message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – Key Physical & Chemical Properties  

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Standard atomic weight** | 1.008 u (average of isotopes) |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H, D), Tritium (^3H, T) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ/mol) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ/mol) |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ/mol) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g/L (0.00008988 kg/m³) |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L/mol |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H₂)** | 436 kJ/mol |
| **Typical bond length (H₂)** | 0.74 Å |
| **Common oxidation states** | +1 (most common), –1 (rarely as hydride H⁻) |
| **Acidity/basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (forming H₃O⁺) or base (forming OH⁻) depending on context |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms covalent bonds with most elements; reacts violently with oxygen (explosive). |
| **Uses** | Fuel cell technology, rocket propellant, laboratory reagent, hydrogenation reactions, ammonia synthesis (Haber process). |

### Quick Facts
- **State at room temperature:** Gas (colorless, odorless, tasteless).
- **Solubility in water:** ~1.6 g per liter at 20 °C (very low).
- **Spectral lines:** Strong Balmer series visible in stellar spectra (Hα, Hβ, etc.).
- **Isotopic significance:** Deuterium used in nuclear fusion research; tritium is radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 years).

These values are standard reference data for hydrogen under normal conditions.
